deep.reconstruction:
PURPOSE. This page is the core of what Siegel (1932) reconstructed from Riemann's Nachlass as the Riemann–Siegel formula. Riemann wants an asymptotic expression for xi on the critical line, s = 1/2 + ti, i.e. for Z(t) (the previous page sets up xi(t) and Stirling for log Pi(s/2)). He combines (i) the first m terms of the Dirichlet series, (ii) a saddle-point treatment of the remainder integral, and (iii) a closed-form evaluation of the resulting Mordell-type integral.

(1) Remainder integral. Riemann writes int_0^oo e^{-mx} x^{s-1}/(e^x-1) dx, which equals Gamma(s) * sum_{n>m} n^{-s} [my gloss]. He takes s-1 = ti - 1/2 and looks for the saddle point of x^{s-1}.
- Put x = alpha + y and expand: (s-1) log(alpha+y) = (s-1)[log alpha + y/alpha - y^2/(2 alpha^2) + y^3/(3 alpha^3) - y^4/(4 alpha^4) + ...].
- He chooses alpha so that the leading quadratic term -ti y^2/(2 alpha^2) equals -y^2/(4 pi i). This gives alpha^2 = -2 pi t, so s - 1 = alpha^2/(2 pi i) - 1/2.
- Substituting, the exponent becomes (alpha^2/(2pi i) - 1/2) log alpha + alpha y/(2pi i) - y^2/(4pi i) + (1/alpha)(-y/2 + y^3/(6pi i)) + (1/alpha^2)(y^2/4 - y^4/(8pi i)) + ...
- The 1/alpha and 1/alpha^2 terms are the seeds of the higher correction terms C1, C2, ... of the Riemann–Siegel expansion.

(2) Shift to the m-th pole. Put x = z + 2m pi i and y = z - alpha + 2m pi i, so the saddle sits near the pole 2m pi i of 1/(e^x - 1). Riemann records the identity 2pi i (alpha/(2pi i) - m)^2 = alpha^2/(2pi i) - 2m alpha + 2 m^2 pi i.
- Keeping the term alpha y/(2pi i), the quadratic term and -mx, the exponent becomes -z^2/(4pi i) + 2 beta z + 2m alpha - (3/4) alpha^2/(pi i) - m^2 pi i.
- Here beta = alpha/(2pi i) - m = sqrt(t/(2pi)) - m.
- He rewrites the constant as -2 pi i beta^2 - (1/4) alpha^2/(pi i) - m^2 pi i. [I checked: both forms equal -3 pi i beta^2 - m alpha modulo 2 pi i Z.]

(3) Evaluation of Q. Define Q = int_L e^{2 beta z - z^2/(4pi i)}/(e^z - 1) dz along a line in direction e^{i pi/4} passing between the poles 0 and 2pi i.
- Shift z = y + 2pi i. Since (y+2pi i)^2/(4pi i) = y^2/(4pi i) + y + pi i, this gives Q = int e^{2 beta y - y^2/(4pi i) + 4 beta pi i - y - pi i}/(e^y - 1) dy + 2pi i e^{4 beta pi i - pi i}. The last term is the residue at 2pi i.
- Because e^{2beta y}/(e^y - 1) - e^{(2beta - 1) y}/(e^y - 1) = e^{(2beta - 1) y}, the denominators cancel. This yields Q(1 + e^{-4 beta pi i}) = int e^{(2beta - 1) y - y^2/(4pi i)} dy - 2 pi i.
- The Fresnel/Gaussian integral is evaluated by completing the square, y -> y - 2pi i(2beta - 1): it equals 2pi e^{i pi/4} e^{(2beta - 1)^2 pi i}.
- Hence Q * 2cos(2 beta pi) e^{-2 beta pi i} = 2pi i (e^{(2beta - 1)^2 pi i - pi i/4} - 1).

(4) Recentering. Put beta = delta + 1/2, so 2beta - 1 = 2delta. Then Q * 2cos(2 delta pi) e^{-2 delta pi i} = 2pi i (e^{4 delta^2 pi i - pi i/4} - 1), the two sign changes cancelling.
- Using e^{i theta} - 1 = 2i sin(theta/2) e^{i theta/2}, he gets e^{4 delta^2 pi i - pi i/4} - 1 = 2 cos(2 delta^2 pi + 3pi/8) e^{2 delta^2 pi i - 5 pi i/8}.
- Therefore Q e^{-2 delta pi i - 2 delta^2 pi i + 5 pi i/8}/(2 pi i) = cos(2 delta^2 pi + 3pi/8)/cos(2 delta pi).
- Completing the square, z - z^2/(4pi i) + 2 delta z - 2 delta^2 pi i - 2 delta pi i = z^2/(4pi i) - 2pi i (delta + 1/2 - z/(2pi i))^2 + pi i/2. Riemann writes the expansion -2pi i(delta^2 + delta) + z(2delta + 1) - z^2/(2pi i) - (1/2) pi i.
- Final form: cos(2 delta^2 pi + 3pi/8)/cos(2 delta pi) = (1/(2pi)) e^{5 pi i/8} int e^{z^2/(4pi i)}/(e^z - 1) * e^{-2pi i (delta + 1/2 - z/(2pi i))^2} dz.
- In beta-form this is cos(2pi(beta^2 - beta) - pi/8)/cos(2 pi beta), exactly Siegel's Psi / C0 function.

(5) Removable singularities (centre right). The zeros of cos(2 delta pi) are at delta = n +- 1/4. There 2 delta^2 = 2n^2 +- n + 1/8, so 2 delta^2 pi + 3pi/8 = (2n^2 +- n) pi + pi/2 and the numerator vanishes too. So the ratio is entire; Riemann's notes 'delta = n +- 1/4, n^2 +- n/2' record this check.

(6) Assembling the main term (lower left).
- The phase/modulus bookkeeping reads (1-s) log(2pi i) - ti + (s-1) log(sqrt(2pi t) i) + ti/2 - m^2 pi i = ((s-1)/2) log(t/(2pi)) + ...
- Its real part gives the factor e^{-(1/4) log(t/(2pi))} = (t/(2pi))^{-1/4}, together with a phase pi/8 - m^2 pi.
- The result is 2 sum_{n=1}^m cos(theta - t log n)/sqrt(n) + (t/(2pi))^{-1/4} e^{(...)pi i} cos((beta^2 - beta) 2pi - pi/8)/cos(2 beta pi).
- With gamma = sqrt(t/(2pi)) - m - 1/2 (= delta), the half-version reads: sum_1^m cos(theta - t log n)/sqrt(n) + (-1)^{m(-1?)} cos(2pi gamma^2 + 3pi/8)/(2 (t/(2pi))^{1/4} cos(2pi gamma)).
- This is Z(t)/2 to leading order, i.e. the Riemann–Siegel formula with the first correction term C0.

(7) Right column. A residue computation: an integral int_oo^0 of (e^{-x}-type)/(...) x^{s-1} dx is evaluated as 2pi sum (n pi i)^{s-1}, i.e. as a sum over poles at x = n pi i. This is a version of Riemann's contour proof of the functional equation (alternating zeta / (1 - 2^{1-s}) variant); it is only partly legible.

(8) Bottom. 't/2 = (9/2) pi' (t = 9pi, sqrt(t/(2pi)) ~ 2.12, m = 2) looks like a numerical test value.
errors: First equality '(1/2pi) Q e^{-2 delta pi i - 2 delta^2 pi i + 5/8 pi i} = cos/cos' is off by a factor i. The correct factor is 1/(2 pi i), or equivalently (1/(2pi)) e^{pi i/8} if the exponent is changed. The next expression '(1/2pi) e^{(1/8 or 5/8) pi i} int ...' and the final boxed formula with (1/(2pi)) e^{5pi i/8} are consistent once the +pi i/2 from completing the square is included. So this is at worst a harmless slip, possibly a transcription issue.

The sign of the remainder term: the standard Riemann–Siegel formula has (-1)^{m-1} (t/2pi)^{-1/4} cos(2pi(p^2-p-1/16))/cos(2pi p) with p = beta. Rewritten in gamma = beta - 1/2 this is (-1)^{m-1} cos(2pi gamma^2 + 3pi/8)/cos(2pi gamma). The transcription shows (-1)^m. Either the exponent is partly obscured by the blot (likely m-1) or this is a sign slip.
Expansion line: the coefficient of y should be alpha y/(2 pi i). The transcription's alpha y/(pi i) is presumably a misreading.
Constant terms are only correct modulo 2 pi i (e.g. -3 m^2 pi i is replaced by -m^2 pi i), which is legitimate inside an exponential.
Higher-order 1/alpha terms are dropped without an error estimate; this is a heuristic leading-order derivation, not a proof (Siegel supplied the rigorous estimates).

results.what: Saddle-point treatment of the remainder int e^{-mx}x^{s-1}/(e^x-1)dx with saddle alpha, alpha^2 = -2 pi t, shifted to the pole 2m pi i, giving the main sum up to m = floor(sqrt(t/2pi))
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (Nachlass), published/proved by C. L. Siegel 1932

results.what: Closed form Q*2cos(2 beta pi)e^{-2 beta pi i} = 2 pi i (e^{(2beta-1)^2 pi i - pi i/4} - 1), equivalently int e^{z^2/(4pi i)}/(e^z-1) e^{-2pi i(delta+1/2-z/2pi i)^2}dz = 2pi e^{-5pi i/8} cos(2 delta^2 pi + 3pi/8)/cos(2 delta pi)
results.modern_name: Mordell integral evaluation / Riemann–Siegel Psi(p) = cos(2pi(p^2-p-1/16))/cos(2pi p)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (via Siegel 1932); Mordell integrals studied by Mordell 1933

results.what: Z(t) ~ 2 sum_{n<=m} cos(theta - t log n)/sqrt(n) + (-1)^{m-1}(t/2pi)^{-1/4} C0(p)
Check that cos(2 delta^2 pi + 3pi/8)/cos(2 delta pi) has removable singularities at delta = n +- 1/4
Residue evaluation of a Mellin integral as 2pi sum (n pi i)^{s-1}
results.modern_name: contour-integral proof of the functional equation

deep.surprise_reason: This is precisely the Nachlass material from which Siegel (1932) extracted the Riemann–Siegel formula and the Mordell-type integral C0. The content is famous and already credited to Riemann. The page is a primary source for a known attribution rather than a new discovery.

transcription_corrections: Line 2 '-t x^2/(2 pi i) - 1/2' should read '= alpha^2/(2 pi i) - 1/2' (expressing s-1 via alpha).
In the exponential expansion the y-coefficient should be alpha y/(2 pi i), not alpha y/(pi i).
'-2 beta[?] pi i beta[?] - 1/4 alpha alpha/(pi i) - mm pi i' is '-2 pi i beta^2 - (1/4) alpha^2/(pi i) - m^2 pi i'.

'4Q 2cos 2 delta pi e^{-2 delta pi i}' is probably 'Q 2cos 2 delta pi ...' (the '4' is likely part of the beta = delta + 1/2 annotation or a mark). The right-hand side should be 2 pi i (e^{4 delta^2 pi i - pi i/4} - 1), with the bracket enclosing the -1.
Middle equality: the exponent of the prefactor in '= (1/2pi) e^{5/8 pi i} int ...' appears in the image as e^{(1/8) pi i}, which is the mathematically correct value there.
'[-...-] 2 sqrt(pi) e^{pi i/4} = y - 2pi i(2beta - 1)' is a substitution note (shift y -> y - 2pi i(2beta - 1)) together with the Gaussian value 2pi e^{pi i/4}.
In the last line the sign factor is likely (-1)^{m-1} (partly obscured), consistent with the standard formula.
Right column 'Pi(s-1) pi^{-s/2} ...' is uncertain; it is more likely Pi(s-1)(1 - 2^{1-s}...) zeta(s) or similar, from a residue proof of the functional equation.
